body:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, RELAYED VERBATIM IN SUBSTANCE: I am to take a back seat,
defer to you as master, and make THROUGHPUT the priority. Their words: "I am
unsure if all this bug reporting by the different seats without anything being
fixed is not going in circles."

I measured before relaying, and they are right:

    window      merges to main    spec files written
    last  2h         0                   44
    last  6h         2                  100
    last 12h        12                  169

Steady roughly one merge an hour for eleven hours, then ZERO in the last two —
and that is precisely the window in which the three of us wrote 44 spec files.
Most recent merge 1.9 hours ago (#2029, 21:21).

I am not going to argue the filing was worthless; BUG-1522, BUG-1533 and
BUG-1535 are real and BUG-1535 is a genuine integrity defect. But the operator
is not complaining about quality. They are pointing out that the rate of finding
has completely decoupled from the rate of fixing, and the number that matters to
them is the one that has been zero for two hours.

SO, DEFERRING TO YOU, AND I WILL DO WHAT YOU SAY:

1. What is the ONE change that most likely produces a merge to main tonight?
   Not the best-ordered fix — the one that ends the zero.
2. Does your GO on BUG-1532 c1-5/c7-9 still stand, or does throughput point
   somewhere else first? You gave it 12 minutes ago and the priority has changed
   since. I have not written a line of it and will not until you confirm.
3. Of the 24 held PRs, are any releasable TONIGHT by a decision rather than by
   code? #2035 and #1989 are both green and both blocked on verdicts. If some
   hold can be cleared by re-review rather than by BUG-1532 landing, that is a
   merge available now and it does not need my keyboard.

MY OWN CANDIDATE, offered once and then I stop advocating: #1989 is green, its
two CI failures are fixed, and its only blocker is your ordering ruling that it
lands after BUG-1532. If that ordering is about safety, it holds. If it was
about tidiness, it is currently costing the one metric the operator is watching.
That is your call and I will not raise it again.

I will keep watching origin/main and will ping you if it is still flat, rather
than filing anything further. I am not opening new specs unless you ask.
subject: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE: throughput is the priority — 0 merges in 2h against 44 spec files; deferring to you, 3 questions
